title: Prove Dashboard configuration and serving in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-413#prove-dashboard-configuration-and-serving-on-vitest

Verdict: Caught.

Story: SEED-413#prove-dashboard-configuration-and-serving-on-vitest (.planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md); plan .planning/slice-plans/868-prove-dashboard-configuration-and-serving-on-vitest/PLAN.md, slice 3 and its Accepted note (child-server checks became in-process recorders in dashboard/backend-tests/support/privateSettingsMachine.ts).
Revision checked: de1d05f0dbf762536c26f20065c89080fa84344e.
Promise: the local OpenAI configuration boundary handles requests without modifying saved files, leaking secrets or making external network requests.

Setup: isolated scratch worktree (git worktree add --detach) at the checked revision under the job tmp directory; real npm ci (217 packages, node_modules a real directory, not a symlink); Node v24.21.0 matching .node-version. Pre-probe state: clean, HEAD = checked revision.
Command (all three runs): caffeinate -s -i env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run test:dashboard:backend -- 'configuration/openai-configuration-boundary\.spec\.ts$' --workers=1
Host load average was about 15-19 during the runs.

Baseline: passed. 1 test file, 1 test ("OpenAI configuration refuses foreign/malformed requests without changing private files or contacting a provider", openai-configuration-boundary.spec.ts:45). The case ran (89 ms); Vitest reported 6.32 s.

Fault (one edit to dashboard/server/openAIConfigurationBoundary.ts, with tests and fixtures unchanged): just before saveOpenAIAPIKey(apiKey) on the save path, the boundary now sends a fire-and-forget request, fetch("https://api.openai.com/v1/models", { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` } }). Its settle handlers append the outcome to a scratch witness file outside the worktree. Because the request is fire-and-forget, the save still returns 200, so earlier status and file assertions cannot hide the fault.

Faulted run: failed at the intended assertion. The test result was:
  AssertionError: expected [ 'api.openai.com' ] to deeply equal []
  at openai-configuration-boundary.spec.ts:149:26, expect(machine.egress).toEqual([]);
No earlier assertion failed. The status, file-unchanged, removal and existsSync assertions all passed before line 149.
Independent wrong-behavior witness: the scratch witness file recorded "rejected Error: External requests are blocked.". This shows that the boundary's save path started an outbound provider request carrying the credential. The in-process fetch spy blocked it. A real server would have contacted api.openai.com.

Reach: the fault is on the valid-save path, which the spec exercises first (saved.status 200). The witness confirms that the faulted line ran. The claim covers only this path: a provider request made through globalThis.fetch while saving a valid key. Requests that bypass globalThis.fetch (for example node:http/https, undici or a child process) are outside what the egress recorder observes. This probe did not test that.

Restoration: the edit was reverted with git checkout (an EXIT trap). git status --porcelain and git diff were empty, and HEAD was still the checked revision. Rerunning the same command passed: 1/1 test (53 ms; Vitest reported 1.40 s). The scratch worktree was then removed with git worktree remove --force. git worktree list no longer shows intent-scratch, and the witness file was deleted. The reviewed checkout was never edited. Its git status shows a pre-existing modification to .planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md that this probe did not make.

Next proof action: none is required for this promise and path. The maintained assertion expect(machine.egress).toEqual([]) catches globalThis.fetch egress from the save path. If wider network coverage is wanted, a separate probe could check egress through node:https or undici, which the recorder does not intercept.
Matching prior disposition: slice 3's Accepted note says each privateSettingsMachine recorder was "shown to fire by a scratch check". This probe independently confirms that for the fetch egress recorder in openai-configuration-boundary.spec.ts. It is recognition of an existing disposition, not a new repair decision.

Costs:
- Test runtime: measured, from Vitest's reported Duration: baseline 6.32 s (cold transform), faulted 1.75 s, restored 1.40 s; about 9.5 s in total. Test case time was 89 / 61 / 53 ms. The npm ci install took about 6 s (npm's report).
- Human effort: unavailable; no human time was recorded for this agent-run probe.
- Agent effort: unavailable; no separate token or turn meter was available to this agent.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 85388 ms (measured), from 1795750924000 to 1795751009388 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: de1d05f0dbf762536c26f20065c89080fa84344e, Caught, no follow-up.
